1.note: The pronoun **he** refers to the man with the measuring reed whom Ezekiel first described in 40:3, not to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the man with the measuring reed brought me out]
By **the way, the way of the north**, Ezekiel means the gate on the north side. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation as in the UST if that would be helpful to your readers.

Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [to the chamber that was in front of the court and to another chamber that was in front of the structure]

2.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Along the front of]

These **cubits** were the long cubits described in 40:5, a unit of measurement corresponding to the distance between an average person’s elbow and middle fingertip plus a handbreadth, or about 54 centimeters or 21 inches. So **100 cubits** was about 54 meters or 175 feet, and **50 cubits** was about 27 meters or 88 feet. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express these distances in modern measurements, either in the text or a footnote. Alternate translation: [100 cubits or 54 meters]

Ezekiel is using the possessive form to describe an **opening** that faces toward the **north**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the opening that faced north]

3.note: Ezekiel is leaving out a word that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply this word from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [In front of the 20 cubits]

These **ledge to a face** could mean: (1) shelves that faced each other, Alternate translation: [was a shelf that faced another shelf] or (2) a kind of gallery or terrace that faced each other along the sides of the building. Alternate translation: [were terraces that faced each other]

By **in the third**, Ezekiel means into three levels of the building. He assumes that readers will know that the chambers were arranged in three stories and that the ledges were between the levels. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [split into three levels]

4.note: Here, **And to the face of** represents being in front of the chambers. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And in front of]

This could mean: (1) that the **passage** was on the north side of the rooms, which would be the **inner** side of the outer courtyard, Alternate translation: [to the inner side of the outer courtyard] or (2) that the **passage** was on the south side of the rooms, on the side facing the temple building, Alternate translation: [along their inner side] or (3) that the **passage** was within the block of rooms. Alternate translation: [between the rows of chambers]

The words translated as **a way of one cubit** represent the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have misspelled the original consonants of the text, resulting in this word. With different spelling, it would say “in length 100 cubits,” which seems to fit better the meaning of this passage. The UST follows that interpretation. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [and 100 cubits in length]

By **their openings were to the north**, Ezekiel means that the doors of the chambers faced the north side, opening onto the walkway that ran along the front of the rooms. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the chambers’ doors faced toward the north side]

5.note: See how you translated the same word, “ledges” in 41:15.

Ezekiel is speaking as if the **ledges ate** part of the upper or **highest chambers.** He means that the ledges took up space that would otherwise have been part of those chambers, so those chambers were narrower than the ones below them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for the ledges took up some of their space]

Ezekiel is using the adjectives **lowers** and **middles** as nouns to mean the lower and middle chambers. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [from the lower chambers and from the middle chambers of the structure]

6.note: Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [For the chambers were built on three levels]

6.q: וְ⁠אֵ֤ין לָ⁠הֶן֙ עַמּוּדִ֔ים כְּ⁠עַמּוּדֵ֖י הַ⁠חֲצֵר֑וֹת עַל־כֵּ֣ן נֶאֱצַ֗ל
6.note: This could mean: (1) that none of the rooms on any story had pillars. Because of this, the higher stories were narrower than the lower stories, Alternate translation: [and there not for the three stories pillars like the pillars of the courtyards. Therefore, the higher stories were withdrawn] or (2) that just the rooms on the third stories did not have pillars. Because of this, the highest story was narrower than the lower two stories. Alternate translation: [and there were not for the highest story pillars like the pillars of the courtyards. Therefore, this highest story was withdrawn]

The expression **it was withdrawn** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could say that the builders did it. Alternate translation: [the builders set the higher chambers back]
See how you translated these same phrase, “from the lowers and from the middles,” in the previous verse.

7.note: By **corresponding to the chambers**, Ezekiel means that the wall ran alongside the chambers, parallel to them and along the outer courtyard. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [running parallel to the chambers along the outer courtyard]
See how you translated the similar expression in 42:2. Alternate translation: [along the front of]

8.q: כִּֽי אֹ֣רֶךְ הַ⁠לְּשָׁכ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֶ⁠חָצֵ֥ר הַ⁠חִֽצוֹנָ֖ה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה וְ⁠הִנֵּ֛ה עַל פְּנֵ֥י הַ⁠הֵיכָ֖ל מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה
8.note: This could mean: (1) that the chambers along the outer wall (see 41:17) were **50 cubits** deep. This accounted for the rest of the **100 cubits** that the chambers on the north side of the courtyard around the **nave** measured. In other words, the 50-cubit wall started from the end of the 50-cubit chamber that backed up against the western outer wall, Alternate translation: [For the length of the chambers in the outer courtyard was 50 cubits, and behold, that plus the wall added up to the length of the rooms that faced the courtyard around the nave, which was 100 cubits] or (2) that there were chambers only for **50 cubits** on the side of the structure that faced the outer courtyard, while there were chambers for **100 cubits** on the side of the structure that faced toward the **nave**. Alternate translation: [For the length of the chambers that faced the outer courtyard was 50 cubits, and behold, those that faced the courtyard around the nave were 100 cubits]

The word translated as **behold** represents the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have added the wrong vowels to the original consonants of the text, resulting in this word. With different vowels, it would say “they,” which seems to fit better the meaning of this passage. The UST follows that interpretation. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [and they were upon the face of the nave, 100 cubits]

Here, **upon the face of** represents being in front of or alongside the nave. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [along the front of]
See how you translated this same word, “the nave,” in [41:1](ta:41).

9.note: Ezekiel assumes that readers will know **from under these chambers** means that the entrance was at the lower level of the chambers, beneath the upper stories. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And from the lowest row of chambers]

By **in his going to them from the outer courtyard**, Ezekiel means that a person would enter the lower chambers by coming in from the outer courtyard through the entrance on the east side. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [as one comes into them from the outer courtyard]

10.note: The phrase **in the width of the wall of the courtyard** could go with: (1) the previous verse as in the UST. In this case, the phrase identifies where the entrance is. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine 42:9 and 42:10 into a verse bridge in order to keep the information about the entrance to the chambers together, or (2) this verse. In this case, the phrase identifies where the set of rooms to the south is. For this alternate translation, end the previous verse with a period. Alternate translation: [In the width of the wall of the courtyard, the way of]

The word **the width** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation, which has “the beginning,” or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [in the beginning of]

The phrase **The way of the east** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation, which reads “south,” or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. (Notice that verse 12 confirms that these duplicate chambers are on the side side of the temple.) Alternate translation: [The way of the south]
See how you translated the same expression, “to the face of,” in 42:2.

11.note: Here, **to their faces** represents being in front of the rooms. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [was in front of them]

The pronoun **their** refers to the chambers that Ezekiel mentioned at the end of the previous verse, not to the chambers on the north side that he mentions next. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And a way was in front of these southern chambers]

The implication is that using **according to** means that what Ezekiel has already described are “the same as” these. You could include this information as in the UST if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated these same phrases in 40:24.

Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Their length was the same as the length of those northern chambers, and their width was the same as the width of those northern chambers]

Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and all of their goings out were like those of the northern chambers, and they had the same ordinances and the same openings as the northern chambers]

The word **ordinances** here refers to the measurements or arrangement of the chambers. If your readers would not be familiar with this use of the word, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and with the same arrangements]

12.q: וּ⁠כְ⁠פִתְחֵ֣י הַ⁠לְּשָׁכ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַ⁠דָּר֔וֹם פֶּ֖תַח
12.note: The phrase **And according to the openings of the chambers that were the way of the south** could go with: (1) what follows. In this case, the opening on the east side of the **way**, or passage or walkway, is like the **openings** of the other chambers. See the UST, or (2) the previous verse. In this case, the **openings** of the southern chambers are like the ones on the north rooms. If you use the following alternate translation, you should end the previous verse with a comma. Alternate translation: [and according to the openings of the chambers that were the way of the south. There was an opening]

Here, **head** represents the beginning of something. The phrase **at the head of the way** refers to the place where the walkway or passage begins. See how you translated the similar expression in 21:19. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [at the beginning of the passage]

Here, **in the face of** represents being in front of or parallel to the protecting wall. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of] or [parallel to]

The implication is that **the protecting wall** was a wall that shielded the chambers or set them apart from the area around them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the wall that set the chambers apart from the area around them]

The word translated as **their going** represents the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have spelled the word slightly wrong, resulting in this word. With different spelling, it would say “his going,” which seems to fit better the meaning of this passage. The UST follows that interpretation. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [in his going] or [as one goes in]

13.note: The pronoun **he** refers to the man with the measuring reed whom Ezekiel first described in 40:3 who is guiding him around the temple buildings. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the man guiding me said]

The implication is that **who are near to Yahweh** means being allowed to approach his altar in order to serve him as priests. (See 40:46.) You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [those who are allowed to come near to the altar of Yahweh in order to minister to him as priests]
See how you translated the same phrase, “to the face of,” in 42:2. Alternate translation: [are along the front of]

13.q: קָדְשֵׁ֣י הַ⁠קֳּדָשִׁ֑ים שָׁ֞ם יַנִּ֣יחוּ קָדְשֵׁ֣י הַ⁠קֳּדָשִׁ֗ים
13.note: The man is using the possessive form to describe **holy things** that are characterized by being even more holy than other **holy things**, specifically the offerings or sacrifices. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. The same expression occurs later in this verse. Alternate translation: [the most holy sacrifices. There they make rest the most holy sacrifices]

13.q: שָׁ֞ם יַנִּ֣יחוּ קָדְשֵׁ֣י הַ⁠קֳּדָשִׁ֗ים וְ⁠הַ⁠מִּנְחָה֙ וְ⁠הַ⁠חַטָּ֣את וְ⁠הָ⁠אָשָׁ֔ם כִּ֥י הַ⁠מָּק֖וֹם קָדֹֽשׁ
13.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that this is the reason for what came before. If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since the place is holy, there they make rest the holy things for the holy things and the grain offering and the sin offering and the guilt offering.]

The man is using **they make rest** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they put” or “they store.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they store]

14.q: בְּ⁠בֹאָ֣⁠ם הַ⁠כֹּהֲנִ֗ים וְ⁠לֹֽא־יֵצְא֤וּ מֵ⁠הַ⁠קֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ אֶל־הֶ⁠חָצֵ֣ר הַ⁠חִיצוֹנָ֔ה וְ⁠שָׁ֞ם יַנִּ֧יחוּ בִגְדֵי⁠הֶ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־יְשָׁרְת֥וּ בָ⁠הֶ֖ן כִּֽי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֑נָּה
14.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that this is the reason for what came before. If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since the clothes the priests wear when they minister are holy, in their going, they do not go out from the holy place to the outer courtyard, but there they make rest their clothes in which they minister.]
See how you translated the same expression, “they make rest,” in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [they should store]
The pronoun **they** refers to the priests’ clothes, not to the priests. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [for those clothes are holy]

The implication is that **what is for the people** refers to the areas of the temple where the people were allowed to go, such as the outer courtyard. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they come near to the areas where the people are allowed to go, such as the outer courtyard]

15.note: This could mean: (1) the area and buildings inside the outer walls, Alternate translation: [the things inside the temple complex] or (2) the Most Holy Place. Alternate translation: [the Most Holy Place] or [the room farthest inside the temple building]

15.q: דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַ⁠שַּׁ֔עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּנָ֖י⁠ו דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַ⁠קָּדִ֑ים
15.note: See how you translated the similar expression, “gate whose face was the way to the east,” in 40:6. Alternate translation: [through the gate that faced east]

Ezekiel is repeating the word **around** in order to intensify the idea that it conveys. He means that the man measured all the way around the outside of the temple area. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. This also occurs throughout the description of this vision. Alternate translation: [all the way around]

16.note: Here, **the wind** represents one of the directions or sides of the world. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the side facing east]

Ezekiel is using the possessive form to describe a **reed** that was used for **measurement**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with the reed that he used for measuring]

The phrase **five cubits** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. There is, however, a correction that reads “500” in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [500 cubits]

17.note: See how you translated these similar expression, “the wind of the east,” in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [the side facing north]
Ezekiel assumes that readers will know that by **500**, he means “500 cubits.” You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [500 cubits]
See how you translated the same expression, “in the reed of the measurement around,” in the previous verse.

18.note: See how you translated these similar expression, “the wind of the east,” in verse 16. Alternate translation: [The side facing south]
See how you translated “500” in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [500 cubits]
See how you translated the similar expression, “in the reed of the measurement around,” in verse 16.

19.note: Here, **the wind of the sea** represents “the west,” since the Mediterranean Sea was to the west of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the side facing west]
See how you translated “500” in verse 17. Alternate translation: [500 cubits]
See how you translated the similar expression, “in the reed of the measurement around,” in verse 16.

20.note: Here, **four winds** represents all four of the directions or sides of the world, north, south, east, and west. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [All four sides of the temple area]
See how you translated the same expression, “around, around,” in verse 15.
See how you translated “500” in verse 17. Alternate translation: [500 cubits and in width 500 cubits]

Here, **to** marks **separate between the holy to common** as the goal or purpose of the **wall** that surrounded the temple area. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [its purpose was to separate between the holy and the common]

Ezekiel is using the adjectives **holy** and **common** as nouns. He could mean: (1) the **holy** area inside the wall and the **common** area outside the wall, Alternate translation: [the holy places to common places] or (2) any **holy** places, things, and people and any **common** places, things, and people. Alternate translation: [holy things to common things]
